diagnostic_summary.phev_consumption_method: UF * (CD electricity plus CD fuel energy) + (1 - UF) * CS fuel energy; ATB range-bucket UF
limitations: Gasoline composition uses MTO families with applicable reviewed identities and positive documentary evidence. Eligible families must cover the configured share of gasoline-compatible family counts in each model-year/size-class cohort; otherwise the class uses its hierarchical catalogue median. Compatible gasoline trims exclude hybrids and alternative fuels, but MTO counts do not observe fuel or trim. This threshold is a coverage policy, not a confidence probability. Coverage of the whole mapped all-fuel class is separate.

iZEV records cover eligible purchases and leases, including program exceptions for demonstrators and repeat incentive requests. These are acquisition records, not identifiable unique vehicles. The supported model-year window and regional/national pooling threshold are recorded in configuration. Earlier target vintages may use that whole window as an explicit composition proxy, paired only with target-year Ratings; those reused records are not observed historical registrations and must not be summed across target vintages. Incentives do not cover the full market; price, vehicle and program eligibility select the observed acquisitions. Request year differs from vehicle model year, so later requests make the composition an ex-post proxy. Identical administrative rows are retained because the public data provide no VIN for vehicle-level deduplication.

Every rated subclass lacking empirical support uses a median across canonical make/model family medians of distinct eligible trims. Original outer class weights remain; only genuinely absent rated classes require renormalization. Each selected source description contributes its count once using its compatible family's median consumption. A clear PEV family uses median eligible-trim range for bucket allocation; this is a representative-rating assumption, not observed trim composition. Contradictory identity, class or explicit configuration remains unresolved and visible.

Count weights stand in for vehicle activity under equal annual distance within each CEUD class: a common VKT factor cancels from the weighted consumption mean. This is a modelling assumption, not evidence that the observed families have equal real-world use.

Each PHEV row combines UF times CD electricity-plus-fuel energy with (1 minus UF) times CS fuel energy, using the ATB range-bucket UF. Family/cohort aggregation follows. Independent operating-mode values remain in tables; CS is not added unweighted to CD. The transferred travel share and laboratory ratings are not measured Canadian consumption.

Existing-period consumption and loads use raw annual cohort counts before lifetime redistribution; service efficiency is calculated last. OMEGA combines supported historical range periods and the recorded cohort anchors future ATB ratios. Historical rating gaps retain explicit existing analogue policies. Annual years after the aligned 2023 reference use bounded ATB consumption interpolation.

Catalogue family medians and the hierarchical cohort median in the grids/heatmap are stages of the current production method. Future plots show only recorded production values and anchors. Detailed ATB classes inherit parent loads and cohort weights. Smoother curves and high matched shares alone do not establish representativeness.

The final StatCan comparison is validation only. Registered stock, new registrations, MTO fit-active survivors and incentivized acquisitions have different populations and reference periods. Calendar request years are not model years. MTO does not observe powertrain: a catalogue-resolved subset cannot establish the full fleet's fuel composition, and non-overlapping years remain labelled.

Medium/heavy truck incumbents use their fuel-specific CEUD fleet cohort through the aligned ATB reference year. Later source observations remain visible in the source views; projected annual values use that cohort and relative ATB consumption changes.

mhdv_partial_charge.text: For example, the 6-vehicle partial charge throughput input for public vehicles which would draw 464 kWh daily on average (6 x 77.3 kWh) is the equivalent of 2 vehicles fully charging and another charging 60%. Similarly, the 2-vehicle partial charge throughput input for private vehicles equates to 154 kWh or a single vehicle throughput charging to 87%. Return to footnote 67 referrer

mhdv_population.text: We mapped the CEUD vehicle categories—medium trucks, heavy trucks, school buses, transit buses, and intercity buses—to the seven truck and four bus segments used in this study (as described in Section 3.1)

mhdv_zev_scrappage.text: We assume a ZEV scrappage rate of 0% due to the lack of data on the typical lifetime of ZE-MHDVs; that is, we assume that all ZEVs remain in the fleet over time.

mhdv_scenarios.text: Three MHDV sales forecast scenarios: Policy Reference (100% by 2040, 35% by 2030); Fast Adoption (35% by 2028); Slow Adoption (35% by 2032).

mhdv_hydrogen_sensitivity.text: We further assume that all MHDVs will be battery-electric vehicles (BEVs), due to a higher degree of technology maturity and a better economic performance in all MHDV segments. Footnote 21 We also perform a sensitivity analysis to assess the extent to which charging needs for BEVs would be reduced if hydrogen-powered vehicles were to see a significant market uptake as a result of lower hydrogen prices.

production_representation.parameter_basis: Five physical archetypes from the shared production core; aggregated mode pools their investment-cost basis and retains separate utilization/stock-rating policies

settings.ldv_scenario: High access to home charging (base case)

limitations: The configured production representation is reported separately from the five physical archetypes used to derive it.
Home utilization is an empirical scenario proxy; residential L2 telemetry is extended to home L1, not a national measurement.
MHDV production uses Table 19 session duration and throughput; battery recharge cases remain research sensitivities without taper or downtime.
The point-year registration stock illustration is an alternative; production uses its prepared physical BEV stock handoff.
National MHDV composition is transferred to provinces; source bus coverage differs from the selected registration classes.
Type-specific hourly charging profiles and joint solver feasibility require separate evidence; an aggregate hourly profile does not establish them.
production_representation.stock_status: Research alternative: direct point-year registrations; production uses prepared physical BEV stock.

stock_calculations.status: Lower bound; some registrations are unpublished

stock_source.scope: BEVs only. LDVs include cars, pickups, multi-purpose vehicles and vans; other LDVs, buses and motorcycles are excluded. Class 3–6 registrations include larger SUVs/pickups and are not a freight-only count.
